column1: # Campaign 27 source evidence for the authenticated prepared point-read TCP route.

column5: The authenticated Rust TCP loop now owns per-connection monotonically allocated statement IDs, prepare/execute/type-reuse/silent-close dispatch, and signed-BIGINT binary rows while executing through the configured real-PD/TiKV session; cursors, long data, reset, NULL, coercion, writes, transactions, and the rest of Go clientConn remain open. Real runtime acceptance belongs to the separate live proof.

The existing worker-local real-TiKV session factory now types prepared point reads against its concrete configured catalog and executes bound ReadOnlyScanPlan values through its retained production transport; the complete Go driver/session interface remains open.

Prepared execution reuses the real session timestamp, cancellation, DistSQL record set, transport evidence, and cleanup authorities instead of a mock or interpolated query path; transactions, writes, plan cache, privilege breadth, and complete TiDB session behavior remain open.

The existing packet reader and command decoder now route raw COM_STMT_PREPARE, COM_STMT_EXECUTE, and COM_STMT_CLOSE payloads into the typed prepared protocol decoder before engine work; complete command and charset parsing parity remains open.

Prepared statements run inside the existing authenticated listener, worker, cancellation, connection accounting, and shutdown lifecycle without another listener or backend authority; the complete Go server service surface remains open.

Prepared handles are scoped below one admitted authenticated TCP connection and disappear with that connection while shared connection accounting remains unchanged; resource groups, dynamic per-account limits, and distributed coordination remain open.
